content:
Fix the starting corner \(A\). Any healthy closed trail in the 3-regular cube graph must be a simple cycle.  
A 4-cycle is a face, using 4 edges of that face, so invalid. An 8-cycle has \(8\cdot2=16\) face-edge incidences, but with 6 faces allowing at most 2 each, max is \(12\), so invalid. Thus only 6-cycles work.

For a 6-cycle, total face-edge incidences is \(6\cdot2=12\), so it must use exactly 2 edges on each face.

At \(A\), choose which two of the three incident edges are used: \(\binom{3}{2}=3\) choices. These two edges determine a face through \(A\), forcing the other two edges of that face to be unused, and this uniquely determines the cycle. So there are \(3\) healthy cycles through \(A\).

Each cycle can be traversed in two directions, so the number of healthy paths is
\[
3\cdot 2 = 6.
\]
\[
\boxed{6}
\]
